newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajikistan's warring sides agree to share power.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan's warring sides agree to share power.

text.p: The government and Islamist rebels in Tajikistan's bitter civil war have agreed to share power, Tajik officials said on Saturday.
The former Soviet republic's president, Imomali Rakhmonov, and opposition leader Sayid Abdullo Nuri signed the power-sharing agreement in the Iranian city of Mashad on Friday.
"It is a great success," Zafar Saidov, Rakhmonov's spokesman, told a news conference in the capital Dushanbe. "They managed to reach agreement on the most difficult questions."
Saidov said the accord gave 13 seats of the new 26-member National Commission for Reconciliation to each side.
The spokesman said Nuri wouldl chair the commission and return to Dushanbe about two weeks after further peace talks scheduled to take place in Moscow on Wednesday.
A special force of around 80 men will be formed from government and opposition forces to protect commission members.

Seven people, including two security guards at the United States embassy in Dushanbe were shot and killed by unidentified gunmen in the capital last week, only a day after the end of a 14-day hostage crisis in which several foreign aid workers were held.

The United States said on Friday it was temporarily evacuating dependents of its embassy staff in Tajikistan because of worsening security in the turbulent Central Asian country, which borders Afghanistan and China.

State Department spokesman Glyn Davies said the move was prompted by the killing by unidentified gunmen of its two embassy guards, locally hired ethnic Russians who Washington says were off-duty at the time.
"That was the trigger for taking this action," Davies told reporters in Washington.

Tajikistan has been devastated by a four-year civil war costing tens of thousands of lives. A ceasefire agreed between the warring sides last December appears to be holding despite continued sporadic violence in the republic.
